http.exception_policy: The 65536-byte default remains for other handlers. Only exact LLD-03 AddWorkingNote POST and EditWorkingNote PATCH routes select the 524288-byte transport ceiling before body buffering; count received bytes even without Content-Length, reject oversize, and retain authentication/CSRF/origin/strict JSON validation. This is not a configurable global override.

sqlite.authoritative_transaction_rule: short BEGIN IMMEDIATE only; no file parsing/network waits/user interaction while write lock held

executors.rule: blocking DB/file work uses bounded host-owned executor and obtains its own verified connection

jobs.dedupe_rule: caller-supplied packet semantic dedupe keys are validated against the registered static job contract, bounded before hashing, never persisted raw by Foundation, and stored only as SOMA_DURABLE_JOB_DEDUPE_V1 lowercase SHA-256 identity

command_replay.rule: Every newly committed command persists its exact canonical response within the default bound or an exact reviewed schema/version allocation in the same UnitOfWork. The value is never truncated. A command whose exact response cannot satisfy its applicable bound fails and rolls back before success; larger command-response contracts require an explicit reviewed bound allocation rather than creating an unreplayable receipt.

response_bound_allocations.derivation: Hierarchy mutation responses contain one root plus the default bounded page of at most 100 children and, when more children exist, one continuation. Under the accepted LLD-04 RFC field byte ceilings, NUL-only/control-line prohibitions, UUID4 evidence identities, signed SQLite integer range, closed status/warning vocabularies and canonical JSON rules, a conservative maximum-content construction including a continuation is 23288983 UTF-8 bytes, depth 4 and 4151 aggregate collection items. The byte construction deliberately uses JSON six-byte escaping for every byte of bounded free text because LLD-04 does not prohibit all non-NUL C0 control characters. 32 MiB/8192/depth-8 is therefore the reviewed technical allocation with margin; it is not a child-count business cap.

AcceptInventoryBulkAction may atomically apply up to 2000 reviewed warehouse memberships. Its exact replay response contains one inventory_batch target ref plus per-membership revisions and, in the conservative case, up to one distinct Fault Tag revision per membership. A 2000-target worst-case response is about 314122 canonical UTF-8 bytes and 4006 aggregate collection items; 512 KiB/depth-8/8192 therefore preserves exact replay with margin and does not change the 2000-target business contract.

command_replay.allocation_rule: The default command-replay bounds apply unless an exact response_schema + response_version tuple is listed in response_bound_allocations. An allocated schema name at an unlisted version is unsupported and must not silently inherit either the elevated allocation or a default fallback. Allocations never authorize truncation, rebuilding replay from current state, or widening a domain page/business cap.

audit.exception_policy: Only exact action/schema/version tuples listed here may exceed the 16384-byte payload or 128-result-ref defaults. Working Note edit/removal receive the 524288-byte body-evidence allocation only; LLD-06 batch classification receives 32768 bytes and at most 500 immutable classification-event refs; LLD-07 Inventory bulk receives 262144 payload bytes for at most 2000 typed payload refs but still uses the ordinary audit result-ref limit. All other validation, sensitivity and data-minimization rules remain in force.

rules: Bounds are technical ceilings, never truncation authority for domain evidence or exact replay results.
Exceeding a bound fails visibly with a stable error or moves work to the owning durable-job contract; data is never silently dropped.
LLD-12 may impose stricter security/diagnostic bounds but may not weaken these persistence/concurrency ceilings without reconciliation.
